The load address `y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1` increments by 128 per thread in the x-warp lane, meaning consecutive threads in a warp access elements 128 floats apart (512 bytes apart) — severely uncoalesced. This causes every load to miss L1 (0% hit rate) and saturates L2 at 97%. The fix is to add tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the load pointer so the compiler recognizes the access pattern and emits 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads. Additionally, wrapping with @triton.autotune explores tile configurations that improve coalescing. The evict_last policy on loads should also be changed to evict_first since there is no L1 reuse (0% hit rate).
